title: Hearing King Oliver in Oklahoma City
summary: Tate compares Oliver's records with Armstrong's, and hears him declining in person at a ballroom with a big band.

bands.name: T. Holder's Twelve Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Okay. Well, when -- this is after I joined the band. Well, King Oliver, I had listened to King Oliver's records and I would listen to Louie and he didn't move me like Louie. He could play, but this was before he developed pyorrhea and all of that. He could play, but his sound wasn't as fat and he didn't have as much punch and he didn't swing as much as Louie. And -- but of course, when I actually heard him in person, he had a big band, he was working out of an agency out of Shawnee, Oklahoma, and he came down to Oklahoma City -- we were over there playing at a ballroom -- and we went to catch him that night and he -- of course, he was declining, he wasn't playing as much as he had played, because he was sort of sick and he was having trouble with his teeth.
